natural_language: Calculate the percentage of total sales for each customer segment relative to overall sales, displaying the segment name and the percentage.
sql_query:
WITH total_sales AS (
    SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS overall_sales
    FROM orders
    WHERE status = 'completed'
), segment_sales AS (
    SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS segment_sales
    FROM customers c, orders o
    WHERE c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND o.status = 'completed'
    GROUP BY c.segment
)
SELECT ss.segment, (ss.segment_sales / ts.overall_sales) * 100 AS sales_percentage
FROM segment_sales ss, total_sales ts;

natural_language: Calculate the total number of items ordered and total order amount for each employee, while excluding employees with no completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_ordered, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 0

natural_language: Select all order items related to product ID 5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE product_id = 5;

natural_language: List all corporate customers who signed up after 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND signup_date > '2021-01-01';

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated by each product in 'completed' orders, filtering products that generated more than $2000 in revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2000

natural_language: Find the top 5 products by total revenue generated from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Identify which products have not been sold at all in the last year, including their category and price.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, p.price FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id AND o.order_date >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 year' WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Find the average quantity of items per order for each segment of customers, only showing segments where the average is over 5.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_items_per_order FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING AVG(oi.quantity) > 5

natural_language: Find all employees who have sold products from more than 5 distinct product categories and list their total sales amount from those categories.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 5

natural_language: Get all orders from the east region employees.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE employee_id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM employees WHERE region = 'east');

natural_language: Determine the top 5 products based on total revenue generated from completed orders by VIP customers, including the product name and total revenue amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Count the number of orders with a total amount greater than the average total amount for all orders and group by customer segment.

natural_language: Calculate the average commission earned by employees per order they processed.

natural_language: List the customers who have made more than 5 orders, alongside their total spending, but only include those from the 'central' region.

natural_language: Get the total amount of each order along with the corresponding customer's email.

natural_language: Show the total revenue from completed orders for each category of products exceeding $2000, along with the category name.

natural_language: Retrieve the status of orders for customers in the 'corporate' segment who have products from the 'furniture' category, counting distinct order statuses.

natural_language: Retrieve the full names and emails of customers who have completed orders, including the order date.

natural_language: List all customer IDs and their respective total number of orders who have spent more than the average total amount of all customers.

natural_language: List the status of all orders along with the corresponding customer names.

natural_language: List the top 3 products by total sales from customers in the retail segment with sales exceeding $1500.

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of orders placed by each customer.

natural_language: List all products that have been sold in orders from retail customers, showing the total revenue from each product.

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue and order count for each customer who has ordered more than 5 times, along with their segment information.

natural_language: Get the average quantity of items per order for each employee handling orders that were completed.

natural_language: List all orders along with the employee names who processed them.

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered by corporate customers, including the total quantity sold and the total revenue generated from these orders.

natural_language: Find the most popular product in terms of quantity sold to retail customers in the central region.

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated by each product category from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Determine the cities in which customers have placed at least 10 orders and the total number of orders from those cities.

natural_language: List all the orders placed by customers from the 'west' region.

natural_language: Show all customers and the total count of orders they have made.

natural_language: Get all VIP customers who have an email ending with 'example.com'.

natural_language: Identify products that are most frequently ordered by customers in the east region, including the total quantity sold.
sql_query:
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold
FROM products p
JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id
WHERE e.region = 'east'

natural_language: Find all products sold by employees in the east region, along with the number of times they were sold and the total revenue.

natural_language: Get the segmentation of the highest spending customer, including their total spent and the total number of orders placed.

natural_language: Retrieve all customers from the 'corporate' segment in 'New York'.

natural_language: List all products with their total quantity sold, but only for products where the total quantity sold is above 50.

natural_language: List all employees working in the 'east' region and their associated completed orders.

natural_language: Find the highest commission earned by employees in each region, along with the corresponding employee names.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.region, e.employee_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * e.commission_rate) = (SELECT MAX(sub.total_commission) FROM (SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.employee_id) AS sub)

natural_language: Retrieve the names and email addresses of all retail customers who have placed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Show customer cities and the number of orders they have placed.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Get the average cost of products sold by each employee and filter to show only those averaging over $50.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(p.cost) AS average_cost FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING AVG(p.cost) > 50

natural_language: Find all products that have a price between $50 and $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 50 AND 100;

natural_language: Show all pending orders made by customers in the 'retail' segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail');

natural_language: Get the total number of distinct products sold by 'corporate' customers and their corresponding revenue across all orders.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS distinct_products, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Get the emails of all VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT email FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip';

natural_language: List customers who have a total order amount exceeding $50,000 along with their signup date and segment type.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.signup_date, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 50000

natural_language: Determine the total sales amount for each product in the 'Home' category that has been sold to corporate customers, only including completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE p.category = 'Home' AND c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name

natural_language: Find products with total sales over $1000 while listing their cost and price, grouped by product name.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.cost, p.price, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name, p.cost, p.price HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: List products that have been ordered and their corresponding order IDs.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, oi.order_id FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id;

natural_language: Find the total sales amount for each segment of customers, including the number of orders placed, and sort the results by the total sales amount in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS number_of_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY total_sales DESC;

natural_language: List customers who have placed more than three orders along with their signup dates.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, customers.signup_date FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.full_name, customers.signup_date HAVING COUNT(orders.order_id) > 3;

natural_language: Find the product with the highest total sales amount in completed orders, including its category.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get a list of customers who signed up after March 1, 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date > '2022-03-01';

natural_language: Determine the total revenue by each employee, grouped by their region, and compute the average revenue per region.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, e.employee_id, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_revenue FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.region, e.employee_id;

natural_language: Find employees who have processed orders with a total amount greater than $1000.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT e.full_name FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.total_amount > 1000;

natural_language: Get the number of products sold in total by each employee and the total amount generated from those sales, filtering for sales made to 'vip' customers only.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Get the names of employees who work in the 'central' region and their respective number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS num_orders FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE employees.region = 'central' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Find the top 5 products by total revenue, only including those that have sold more than 100 units.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Get the total amount of each order along with the corresponding employee's full name.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.total_amount, e.full_name FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id;

natural_language: Find employees with a commission rate less than 5%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate < 0.05;

natural_language: List all retail customers who have made completed orders, along with their email.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, customers.email FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'retail' AND orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get all pending orders placed by a specific customer (customer_id = 1).
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND customer_id = 1;

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales figures for each product category sold by corporate customers, with a minimum total sale value of $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Get all orders with a total amount less than $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount < 100;

natural_language: Get the product names and their total sold quantity for products from the 'electronics' category where the total quantity sold is more than 100.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: List the top 3 most popular products based on quantity sold across all orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Select all products that have a price greater than 1000.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > 1000;

natural_language: Retrieve the highest revenue product for each employee in the central region, based on completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE e.region = 'central' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name, p.product_name ORDER BY revenue DESC;

natural_language: List the total number of products sold per category where the sales amount is greater than $1,500.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1500

natural_language: Find the total number of products sold along with the order status.
sql_query: SELECT o.status, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.status;

natural_language: Find the products along with the total number of times they have been ordered.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_ordered FROM products JOIN order_items ON products.product_id = order_items.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name;

natural_language: Find the most popular product based on total quantity sold for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment, p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC;

natural_language: Find the average total amount spent by customers in the VIP segment for each employee, but only include employees who have handled at least 10 orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_spent FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 10

natural_language: Retrieve the orders with a total amount less than or equal to $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount <= 100;

natural_language: Show all completed orders made by customer with ID 42.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42 AND status = 'completed';

natural_language: Count how many products have a price greater than $100.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE price > 100;

natural_language: List all products and their respective categories that have been ordered at least once.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT products.product_name, products.category FROM products JOIN order_items ON products.product_id = order_items.product_id;

natural_language: Find the highest price product ordered by any customer.
sql_query: SELECT MAX(p.price) AS highest_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id;

natural_language: Find the total amount from all completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of orders and the corresponding customer's city for all cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT orders.total_amount, customers.city FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Get the list of products that have been ordered by at least 10 different customers, along with the count of unique customers for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customer_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) >= 10

natural_language: Find all retail customers in the city 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail' AND city = 'New York';

natural_language: Identify customers who have ordered products in more than three different categories, along with the total number of their orders and total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS different_categories, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Find the order IDs and their respective total amounts for pending orders belonging to VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, orders.total_amount FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' AND customers.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of all completed orders along with the order date.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_date, o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Show the order IDs and total amounts for orders placed by customers in the city of 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: List the top products by total revenue, but include only those that have been sold at least 10 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: List customer names along with the order dates in which they ordered products.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Fetch the average quantity of items ordered per completed order for each product, highlighting products sold more than 10 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 10

natural_language: Show products that are in the 'Clothing' category and cost less than $10.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Clothing' AND cost < 10;

natural_language: Get the total revenue generated from each product category for orders placed in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) as total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Identify the products that have the highest total cost in orders, and show how much profit was made from those products.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * (oi.unit_price - p.cost)) AS total_profit FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_profit DESC;

natural_language: Get the full names of all customers who are in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail';

natural_language: List all completed orders made by a specific customer using customer ID 1.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 1 AND status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the customers who have products in orders that exceed the average order total of all completed orders.
sql_query: WITH avg_order AS (SELECT AVG(total_amount) AS average_total FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed') SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.total_amount > (SELECT average_total FROM avg_order);

natural_language: Get the total number of orders placed by customers in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(orders.order_id) AS vip_order_count FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Get all products that cost less than $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost < 100;

natural_language: Find the product that has the highest profit margin (price - cost) in orders placed by corporate customers, along with its sales count.
sql_query: WITH product_profit AS (SELECT p.product_id, (p.price - p.cost) AS profit_margin FROM products p) SELECT p.product_id, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS sales_count FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN product_profit p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY MAX(p.profit_margin) DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold and total revenue for each product id for products with a sale total above 500.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Get a list of products that have been ordered by VIP customers along with the total quantity sold and the average sale price.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_sale_price FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders made by employees in the central region.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE employee_id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM employees WHERE region = 'central');

natural_language: Find the highest total amount ordered by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT MAX(orders.total_amount) AS highest_amount FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Get the total count of orders made by each customer in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Find total order amounts for orders placed before March 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM orders WHERE order_date < '2023-03-01';

natural_language: List all pending orders along with the city of the customers who placed them.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, orders.order_date, customers.city FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Find the number of orders and the average total amount per order for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment

natural_language: Get a summary of total products sold per category in the last year for customers in the VIP segment, along with the total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the employee with the highest commission rate who has sold products in the 'electronics' category, along with the total number of orders they processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate, COUNT(o.order_id) as total_orders FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY e.commission_rate DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Identify the products that are sold by more than 3 employees, including the total number of employees for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.employee_id) AS employee_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.employee_id) > 3

natural_language: Select all employees with a commission rate higher than 5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate > 5;

natural_language: Find the total number of customers and their average order value for each employee, filtering for employees with more than 5 orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_value FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Find the customer who has placed the highest number of orders, along with the state they reside in.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.city ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Find total sales and order count per product, only for products that have been sold in more than 10 orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 10

natural_language: List the average commission earned by employees in each region, grouped by their region.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, AVG(e.commission_rate) AS avg_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Identify the average cost of products sold for each employee based on the total revenue from their orders, but only include employees with over $10,000 in order revenue.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(p.cost) AS average_product_cost FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000

natural_language: Get the names of all products in the 'Electronics' category.
sql_query: SELECT product_name FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics';

natural_language: Get all orders placed by customers with an email containing 'gmail.com'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE email LIKE '%gmail.com%');

natural_language: Get all completed orders made in the year 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2023;

natural_language: List all the completed orders with the order date and the full name of the customer who made them.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_date, customers.full_name FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get all orders and join them with detailed employee information for a specific order status.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, employees.full_name, orders.total_amount FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Get the revenue generated by each segment, along with the total number of orders per segment, sorted by revenue in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

natural_language: Calculate the total cost of products sold for each segment type of customers, along with the total number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(p.cost * oi.quantity) AS total_cost, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List the top three customers who have placed the most orders and their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS num_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY num_orders DESC, total_spent DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Find the total sales amount for each employee based on the completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Find the top 5 customers who have purchased the highest number of items, including their total number of items and total spent.
sql_query:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name
ORDER BY total_items DESC
LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Find out which products have the highest margin (price - cost) sold by 'east' region employees, along with their sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) as sales_amount, (p.price - p.cost) as margin FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY p.product_name, margin ORDER BY margin DESC;

natural_language: List all customers who have made no purchases.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE customer_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders);

natural_language: Find the average number of products per order for all pending orders categorized by their corresponding employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, AVG(item_count) AS avg_products_per_order FROM employees e JOIN (SELECT o.order_id, o.employee_id, COUNT(oi.product_id) AS item_count FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY o.order_id, o.employee_id) AS order_group ON e.employee_id = order_group.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name;

natural_language: List the top 5 products with the highest total sales amount within the 'retail' segment, along with the total sales amount and the number of orders they were included in.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Identify the top 5 products by total sales amount in completed orders, along with the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Find customers with orders that are either completed or cancelled.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status IN ('completed', 'cancelled');

natural_language: List products that are priced at $20 or more.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price >= 20;

natural_language: List employees along with the number of different product categories they have sold and the total sales amount from those categories.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Show all completed orders made in March 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date BETWEEN '2021-03-01' AND '2021-03-31';

natural_language: List all VIP customers and their respective order statuses.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.status FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Find all products with a price less than or equal to $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price <= 30;

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of distinct products ordered by each customer segment and the corresponding total revenue for those products in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS distinct_products, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the list of completed orders and their total amounts along with employee names.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.total_amount, e.full_name FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the total amount for orders made in the year 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND order_date < '2024-01-01';

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales and count of unique products sold by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_sold, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List the customer segments that have made purchases in at least 3 distinct cities, along with the count of different cities they have purchased from.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT c.city) AS city_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.city) >= 3

natural_language: Determine the average commission rate of employees who have processed more than 20 orders in total.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(e.commission_rate) AS average_commission_rate FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 20

natural_language: List all products sold, the total quantity sold, and the total sales amount, but only include products that have total sales above $10000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 10000

natural_language: Identify the orders that include products from three different categories and calculate the total amount spent on those orders.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_amount FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) >= 3

natural_language: Find employees who have handled more than 10 orders and their corresponding total commission earned.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_handled, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 10

natural_language: List products ordered along with their quantities and corresponding order IDs.
sql_query: SELECT oi.order_id, p.product_name, oi.quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id;

natural_language: Find distinct product categories and their respective total sales for products sold by employees in the east region.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the average order amount for customers in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Retrieve all employees with the name 'John Doe'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE full_name = 'John Doe';

natural_language: Count all customers in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Get the number of unique products sold and total revenue from the west region employees for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_sold, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE e.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get orders placed on or after March 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2023-03-01';

natural_language: Show total sales by region for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.region, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.region;

natural_language: Get all retail customers who signed up after January 1, 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail' AND signup_date > '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Show the total order amounts for all customers who signed up in 2022.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.signup_date) = 2022 GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Find all orders placed by a customer with email 'example@example.com'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE email = 'example@example.com');

natural_language: Identify the three most frequently purchased products and their purchase count in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p INNER JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id INNER JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Show all customers who have made purchases but are not from the corporate segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders) AND segment != 'corporate';

natural_language: Determine which products have the highest revenue generated from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

natural_language: Find all order items from order ID 101.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 101;

natural_language: Determine which region has the highest total sales and also get their corresponding employee names.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.region ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Find customers who have never cancelled an order along with their total orders count.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status != 'cancelled' OR o.status IS NULL GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Show the total sales amount for each product sold along with its category.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name, p.category;

natural_language: Get the average order total for the VIP segment customers.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and their statuses for each customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.status, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, o.status;

natural_language: Find customers who bought 'clothing' products and calculate the percentage of their total spending compared to all customers' spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS customer_spending, (SUM(o.total_amount) / (SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM orders)) * 100 AS spending_percentage FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'clothing' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name;

natural_language: Report the top 10 customers by total amount spent on orders, along with their respective signup dates.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, c.signup_date ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 10;

natural_language: Get all products that have a price of exactly $29.99.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 29.99;

natural_language: Determine the most popular product (by quantity sold) in the retail segment, along with the total revenue it generated.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: List all products in a specific category along with their price and cost.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.price, p.cost FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics';

natural_language: Get the latest order date for each customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: List customers and their registration date who have orders marked as cancelled.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, customers.signup_date FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Retrieve order items for a specific order ID, say 102.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 102;

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue contributed by the top 5 products based on sales quantity.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY oi.product_id ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity) DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Identify the products that sold more than 50 units in total, grouped by category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Find all products in the 'Clothing' category with a price below $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Clothing' AND price < 30;

natural_language: Find the total count of products sold and total sales amount for each employee, filtered to only include employees who have sold over $5,000.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Retrieve the most expensive product sold in completed orders along with the customer details.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, MAX(oi.unit_price) as max_price, c.full_name FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, c.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total sales amount for each product by joining order items with products.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the total revenue generated by each category of products from completed orders, including product categories and their corresponding total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Show all orders made after December 1, 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > '2021-12-01';

natural_language: Find the average spending per order for each customer segment, along with the total number of orders per segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_spending, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List each product category and the maximum price of products sold in completed orders, filtering for categories where the maximum price exceeds $100.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, MAX(p.price) AS max_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING MAX(p.price) > 100

natural_language: List the total number of orders and their statuses for employees in the 'west' region.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, o.status, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY e.full_name, o.status;

natural_language: Find all corporate segment customers who signed up in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND signup_date >= '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Find the average quantity of products ordered per category for completed orders, where the average exceeds 10.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated by orders in each city, along with the city name and the number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: List all products within the 'furniture' category.
sql_query: SELECT product_name FROM products WHERE category = 'furniture';

natural_language: Identify the products that have been ordered more than 10 times.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name HAVING SUM(order_items.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Get the average price of products ordered by each customer from the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_product_price FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Get the details of the employees with employee_id 5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE employee_id = 5;

natural_language: Get the names and emails of all customers who are in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT full_name, email FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders made by customers from Los Angeles.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE city = 'Los Angeles');

natural_language: Retrieve customer segments and their corresponding signup dates.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.segment, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders where the total amount is exactly $150.
