natural_language: Identify which customers have never made a purchase, along with the total number of purchases made by others in their segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_purchases_in_segment FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) = 0

natural_language: Find the average total amount of completed orders by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, AVG(orders.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated from completed orders that included products from the 'Electronics' category and group by order date.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_date, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_date

natural_language: Identify segments with the highest total order amount and their respective number of orders, ordered by amount descending.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS number_of_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY total_order_amount DESC;

natural_language: Find all retail customers who signed up after January 1, 2020.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail' AND signup_date > '2020-01-01';

natural_language: Find all completed orders made in the month of December 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 12 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2022;

natural_language: Retrieve the average order amount and the count of orders for each city, but only for cities where the average order amount exceeds 500.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 500

natural_language: List all customers who have not made any orders, with a count of the orders they have (should return zero).
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COALESCE(COUNT(o.order_id), 0) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: Get a list of customers and their signup dates who have not made any orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.signup_date FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Retrieve the average cost of products sold by segment, showing how much revenue is generated from each product segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(p.cost) AS average_product_cost, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Show all customers who signed up in the year 2020.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2020;

natural_language: Get the total cost of all products sold in orders that were completed by employees in the 'central' region, and group by the product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND e.region = 'central' GROUP BY p.category

natural_language: Summarize total sales and number of orders for each product sold in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales amount for each product category that has sold more than $1000 in total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Find the employees who have the most diverse set of orders by the number of unique customers they have served and their total commissions from those orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customers, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY unique_customers DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Show the average order value for each product category from orders that were cancelled, distinguishing between retail and corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_cancellation_value FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category, c.segment;

natural_language: Show the total revenue generated by each product that has been sold in the last 6 months.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 month' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: List the employees who have not made any sales and count how many customers they are assigned to.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM employees AS e LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) = 0

natural_language: Calculate the total count of orders and total sales for each product category sold to customers in the east region.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY p.category

natural_language: Find all employees in the east region with a commission rate greater than 15%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'east' AND commission_rate > 0.15;

natural_language: Get the list of products sold with their respective total sales, ordered by the total sales amount in descending order, but only for orders made by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC;

natural_language: Get the list of customers and their recent order dates.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_date DESC;

natural_language: List all customers who made purchases of products in the 'electronics' category and calculate the total spent by each customer, only including completed orders. Provide customer IDs, names, and total spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name

natural_language: Retrieve orders that were created on March 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-03-01';

natural_language: Retrieve the full names and email addresses of customers who have placed orders and their order statuses.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, o.status FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Get a list of customers who have ordered products from multiple categories, showing their name and the count of different categories.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 1

natural_language: Get a list of all products that have been sold by employees from the central region, including total sales for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Get the average commission rate for employees who sold products in the 'electronics' category where orders have been completed, grouped by region.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, AVG(e.commission_rate) AS average_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Display the full name of corporate customers who spent more than $1000.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'corporate' AND orders.total_amount > 1000;

natural_language: Get the list of all products that were sold at a loss (where selling price is less than cost).
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, (p.cost - p.price) AS loss FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) < SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost)

natural_language: Identify the top 3 products sold by revenue in completed orders and how many times each product was sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get the average total amount of all orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders;

natural_language: Get all orders placed on or after September 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2023-09-01';

natural_language: Get the most popular product category based on total sales amount across all orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Get the total number of items sold and the total revenue from completed orders grouped by category of products.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get a list of all products and the total quantities sold.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity) as total_sold FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name;

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold and the average revenue per product for the 'electronics' category, filtering the results for orders that are completed.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(oi.product_id) AS total_products_sold, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_revenue_per_product FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the total sales amount for each type of customer segment (retail, corporate, vip) from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Determine the total expenses incurred by products sold for cancelled orders, grouped by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(p.cost * oi.quantity) AS total_expenses FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and total revenue per customer city, but only include cities that have more than 5 orders placed.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Calculate the total commission earned by employees based on the sales from completed orders for products in the 'Electronics' category, and return the top 10 employees by commission.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY total_commission DESC LIMIT 10;

natural_language: Retrieve the total quantity of products ordered and total revenue generated from completed orders in the Central region, grouped by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.employee_id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM employees WHERE region = 'central') GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and the total sales for each product, but only include products that have generated more than $1,000 in sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Find the highest selling product in terms of total revenue generated, including the category of that product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Fetch the email addresses of customers who made pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.email FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who signed up in the month of January 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= '2023-01-01' AND signup_date < '2023-02-01';

natural_language: Find the average total amount of orders placed by all customers from 'Chicago'.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Chicago';

natural_language: Find employees with a commission rate higher than 10%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate > 0.10;

natural_language: Calculate the percentage of completed orders versus total orders for each employee, sorted from highest to lowest.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, (COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) / COUNT(o.order_id)) * 100 AS completed_percentage FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY completed_percentage DESC;

natural_language: Get the count of orders per employee, along with their total earnings from commissions, ordered by the number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name ORDER BY order_count DESC

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue from completed orders for each product but only include products that sold more than 50 units in total.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Find the top 3 products with the highest total quantity sold across all orders in the system, but only include products with sold quantity greater than 50.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50 ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 3

natural_language: List each product along with the total revenue generated from it, but only include products that have generated more than $1500 in sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1500

natural_language: Find products priced at exactly $19.99.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 19.99;

natural_language: Retrieve the list of customers who have ordered products from at least two different categories, along with their email addresses.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) >= 2;

natural_language: Find the average total amount of orders for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) as average_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Count the number of unique products sold in completed orders categorized by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the total sales and distinct customers for each product category, only for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders placed by customers in the 'retail' segment.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(orders.order_id) AS retail_orders FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: List the total number of orders by each segment type of customers.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Get products that belong to the 'furniture' category.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'furniture';

natural_language: Find the customer segments that have an average order amount more significant than the overall average order amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders)

natural_language: Find all orders made on March 10, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-03-10';

natural_language: Fetch the list of completed orders along with the corresponding customer emails.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, customers.email FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the quantity of products ordered along with the name of the corresponding product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, oi.quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id;

natural_language: Find all orders made by customer with ID 23.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 23;

natural_language: Count the total number of employees in the west region.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_west_employees FROM employees WHERE region = 'west';

natural_language: List the distinct segments of customers who have placed orders for products in the 'electronics' category, including the count of such customers per segment.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get all customers who signed up in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: List total sales for each product category, where the total sales exceed $5000 in completed orders only.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 5000

natural_language: List the distinct order statuses from orders placed by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT o.status FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Calculate the average order value per customer segment and the total number of orders for each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment

natural_language: Retrieve the employees who sold products worth more than $100,000, along with their total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 100000

natural_language: Retrieve all VIP customers who signed up in the year 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip' AND signup_date >= '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Get a summary of total sales and the number of completed orders for each product, focusing only on those that are in the 'furniture' category.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'furniture' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Get the top 5 products sold in terms of revenue for retail customers, including the total quantity sold and the revenue generated from each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Get all products with a category of 'home goods'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'home goods';

natural_language: Retrieve all orders that were processed by employee ID 3.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE employee_id = 3;

natural_language: Get a list of customers along with the total number of products they have ordered and the total amount spent, but only include those who have spent more than $1,000.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(oi.product_id) AS total_products_ordered, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 1000

natural_language: Get the daily sales figures for the top three products, sorted by total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, DATE(o.order_date) AS sales_date, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS daily_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, sales_date ORDER BY daily_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Retrieve all order items for a specific order ID of 1001.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 1001;

natural_language: List all customers with their total spending if they have made any orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.full_name HAVING NOT SUM(orders.total_amount) IS NULL

natural_language: List the total amount of orders placed by customers in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';
